title: The new bionics that let us run, climb and dance
speaker: Hugh Herr

sentences.en: Looking deeply inside nature, through the magnifying glass of science, designers extract principles, processes and materials that are forming the very basis of design methodology.
From synthetic constructs that resemble biological materials, to computational methods that emulate neural processes, nature is driving design.
Design is also driving nature. In realms of genetics, regenerative medicine and synthetic biology, designers are growing novel technologies, not foreseen or anticipated by nature.
Bionics explores the interplay between biology and design.
As you can see, my legs are bionic. Today, I will tell human stories of bionic integration; how electromechanics attached to the body, and implanted inside the body
are beginning to bridge the gap between disability and ability, between human limitation and human potential.
Bionics has defined my physicality. In 1982, both of my legs were amputated due to tissue damage from frostbite, incurred during a mountain-climbing accident.
At that time, I didn't view my body as broken.
I reasoned that a human being can never be "broken."
Technology is broken. Technology is inadequate.
This simple but powerful idea was a call to arms, to advance technology for the elimination of my own disability, and ultimately, the disability of others.
I began by developing specialized limbs that allowed me to return to the vertical world of rock and ice climbing.

I quickly realized that the artificial part of my body is malleable; able to take on any form, any function -- a blank slate for which to create, perhaps, structures that could extend beyond biological capability.
I made my height adjustable. I could be as short as five feet or as tall as I'd like.
(Laughter) So when I was feeling bad about myself, insecure, I would jack my height up.
(Laughter) But when I was feeling confident and suave, I would knock my height down a notch, just to give the competition a chance.
(Laughter) (Applause) Narrow-edged feet allowed me to climb steep rock fissures, where the human foot cannot penetrate, and spiked feet enabled me to climb vertical ice walls,
without ever experiencing muscle leg fatigue.
Through technological innovation, I returned to my sport, stronger and better.
Technology had eliminated my disability, and allowed me a new climbing prowess.
As a young man, I imagined a future world where technology so advanced could rid the world of disability, a world in which neural implants would allow the visually impaired to see.
A world in which the paralyzed could walk, via body exoskeletons.
Sadly, because of deficiencies in technology, disability is rampant in the world.
This gentleman is missing three limbs. As a testimony to current technology, he is out of the wheelchair, but we need to do a better job in bionics, to allow, one day, full rehabilitation
for a person with this level of injury. At the MIT Media Lab, we've established the Center for Extreme Bionics.

The mission of the center is to put forth fundamental science and technological capability that will allow the biomechatronic and regenerative repair of humans, across a broad range of brain and body disabilities.
sentences.zh: 该中心的使命是提供基础科学和技术能力，使人类能够针对广泛的大脑和身体残疾进行生物机电和再生修复。

sentences.en: Today, I'm going to tell you how my legs function, how they work, as a case in point for this center.
sentences.zh: 今天，我将告诉你们我的腿是如何运作的，它们是如何工作的，作为这个中心的一个例子。

sentences.en: Now, I made sure to shave my legs last night, because I knew I'd be showing them off.
sentences.zh: 现在，我昨晚一定要刮腿毛，因为我知道我会炫耀它们。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Bionics entails the engineering of extreme interfaces.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 仿生学需要极端界面的工程设计。

sentences.en: There's three extreme interfaces in my bionic limbs: mechanical, how my limbs are attached to my biological body; dynamic, how they move like flesh and bone; and electrical, how they communicate with my nervous system.
sentences.zh: 我的仿生肢体有三个极端的接口：机械的，我的肢体如何附着在我的生物身体上；动态，它们如何像肉和骨头一样移动；和电气，它们如何与我的神经系统沟通。

sentences.en: I'll begin with mechanical interface. In the area of design, we still do not understand how to attach devices to the body mechanically.
sentences.zh: 我将从机械接口开始。在设计领域，我们仍然不了解如何将设备机械地连接到身体上。

sentences.en: It's extraordinary to me that in this day and age, one of the most mature, oldest technologies in the human timeline, the shoe, still gives us blisters.
sentences.zh: 对我来说很不寻常的是，在当今时代，人类历史上最成熟、最古老的技术之一——鞋子，仍然给我们带来水泡。

sentences.en: How can this be? We have no idea how to attach things to our bodies.
sentences.zh: 怎么会这样呢？我们不知道如何将东西固定在我们的身体上。

sentences.en: This is the beautifully lyrical design work of Professor Neri Oxman at the MIT Media Lab, showing spatially varying exoskeletal impedances, shown here by color variation in this 3D-printed model.
sentences.zh: 这是麻省理工学院媒体实验室 Neri Oxman 教授的精美抒情设计作品，展示了空间变化的外骨骼阻抗，在此通过 3D 打印模型中的颜色变化来显示。

sentences.en: Imagine a future where clothing is stiff and soft where you need it, when you need it, for optimal support and flexibility, without ever causing discomfort.
sentences.zh: 想象一下未来，衣服在您需要的地方、在您需要的时候既硬又软，以获得最佳的支撑和灵活性，而不会造成不适。

sentences.en: My bionic limbs are attached to my biological body via synthetic skins with stiffness variations, that mirror my underlying tissue biomechanics.
sentences.zh: 我的仿生肢体通过硬度变化的合成皮肤连接到我的生物身体，这反映了我的底层组织生物力学。

sentences.en: To achieve that mirroring, we first developed a mathematical model of my biological limb.
sentences.zh: 为了实现这种镜像，我们首先开发了我的生物肢体的数学模型。

sentences.en: To that end, we used imaging tools such as MRI, to look inside my body, to figure out the geometries and locations of various tissues.
sentences.zh: 为此，我们使用 MRI 等成像工具来观察我的身体内部，找出各种组织的几何形状和位置。

sentences.en: We also took robotic tools -- here's a 14-actuator circle that goes around the biological limb.
sentences.zh: 我们还采用了机器人工具——这是一个围绕生物肢体的 14 个执行器圆圈。

sentences.en: The actuators come in, find the surface of the limb, measure its unloaded shape, and then they push on the tissues to measure tissue compliances at each anatomical point.
sentences.zh: 执行器进入，找到肢体的表面，测量其卸载的形状，然后推动组织以测量每个解剖点的组织顺应性。

sentences.en: We combine these imaging and robotic data to build a mathematical description of my biological limb, shown on the left.
sentences.zh: 我们结合这些成像和机器人数据来构建我的生物肢体的数学描述，如左图所示。

sentences.en: You see a bunch of points, or nodes? At each node, there's a color that represents tissue compliance.
sentences.zh: 您看到一堆点或节点吗？每个节点都有一种代表组织顺应性的颜色。

sentences.en: We then do a mathematical transformation to the design of the synthetic skin, shown on the right.
sentences.zh: 然后，我们对合成皮肤的设计进行数学转换，如右图所示。

sentences.en: And we've discovered optimality is: where the body is stiff, the synthetic skin should be soft, where the body is soft, the synthetic skin is stiff, and this mirroring occurs across all tissue compliances.
sentences.zh: 我们发现最优性是：在身体僵硬的地方，合成皮肤应该是柔软的，在身体柔软的地方，合成皮肤应该是僵硬的，并且这种镜像发生在所有组织顺应性上。

sentences.en: With this framework, we've produced bionic limbs that are the most comfortable limbs I've ever worn.
sentences.zh: 通过这个框架，我们生产出了仿生肢体，这是我佩戴过的最舒适的肢体。

sentences.en: Clearly, in the future, our clothing, our shoes, our braces, our prostheses, will no longer be designed and manufactured using artisan strategies, but rather, data-driven quantitative frameworks.
sentences.zh: 显然，未来我们的衣服、鞋子、牙套、假肢将不再使用工匠策略设计和制造，而是使用数据驱动的定量框架。

sentences.en: In that future, our shoes will no longer give us blisters.
sentences.zh: 将来，我们的鞋子将不再给我们带来水泡。

sentences.en: We're also embedding sensing and smart materials into the synthetic skins.
sentences.zh: 我们还将传感和智能材料嵌入到合成皮肤中。

sentences.en: This is a material developed by SRI International, California.
sentences.zh: 这是由加利福尼亚州 SRI International 开发的材料。

sentences.en: Under electrostatic effect, it changes stiffness.
sentences.zh: 在静电作用下，它会改变刚度。

sentences.en: So under zero voltage, the material is compliant, it's floppy like paper.
sentences.zh: 因此，在零电压下，该材料是合规的，它像纸一样软。

sentences.en: Then the button's pushed, a voltage is applied, and it becomes stiff as a board.
sentences.zh: 然后按下按钮，施加电压，它就会变得像一块木板一样坚硬。

sentences.en: (Tapping sounds) We embed this material into the synthetic skin that attaches my bionic limb to my biological body.
sentences.zh: （敲击声）我们将这种材料嵌入到合成皮肤中，将我的仿生肢体连接到我的生物身体上。

sentences.en: When I walk here, it's no voltage. My interface is soft and compliant.
sentences.zh: 当我走到这里时，没有电压。我的界面柔软且合规。

sentences.en: The button's pushed, voltage is applied, and it stiffens, offering me a greater maneuverability over the bionic limb.
sentences.zh: 按下按钮，施加电压，它就会变硬，为我提供了比仿生肢体更大的可操作性。

sentences.en: We're also building exoskeletons. This exoskeleton becomes stiff and soft in just the right areas of the running cycle, to protect the biological joints from high impacts and degradation.
sentences.zh: 我们还在制造外骨骼。这种外骨骼在跑步周期的适当区域变得坚硬和柔软，以保护生物关节免受高冲击和退化。

sentences.en: In the future, we'll all be wearing exoskeletons in common activities, such as running.
sentences.zh: 未来，我们都将在日常活动中佩戴外骨骼，例如跑步。

sentences.en: Next, dynamic interface. How do my bionic limbs move like flesh and bone?
sentences.zh: 接下来，动态界面。我的仿生肢体如何像肉和骨头一样移动？

sentences.en: At my MIT lab, we study how humans with normal physiologies stand, walk and run.
sentences.zh: 在我的麻省理工学院实验室，我们研究生理正常的人类如何站立、行走和跑步。

sentences.en: What are the muscles doing, and how are they controlled by the spinal cord?
sentences.zh: 肌肉在做什么，它们是如何受脊髓控制的？

sentences.en: This basic science motivates what we build.
sentences.zh: 这一基础科学激发了我们的建设。

sentences.en: We're building bionic ankles, knees and hips.
sentences.zh: 我们正在建造仿生脚踝、膝盖和臀部。

sentences.en: We're building body parts from the ground up.
sentences.zh: 我们正在从头开始构建身体部位。

sentences.en: The bionic limbs that I'm wearing are called BiOMs.
sentences.zh: 我佩戴的仿生肢体被称为 BiOM。

sentences.en: They've been fitted to nearly 1,000 patients, 400 of which have been wounded U.S. soldiers.
sentences.zh: 它们已安装在近 1,000 名患者身上，其中 400 名是受伤的美国士兵。

sentences.en: How does it work? At heel strike, under computer control, the system controls stiffness, to attenuate the shock of the limb hitting the ground.
sentences.zh: 它是如何运作的？脚跟着地时，在计算机控制下，系统控制刚度，以减弱肢体撞击地面的冲击力。

sentences.en: Then at mid-stance, the bionic limb outputs high torques and powers to lift the person into the walking stride, comparable to how muscles work in the calf region.
sentences.zh: 然后，在中间站立时，仿生肢体会输出高扭矩和功率，将人提升到迈步状态，类似于小腿区域肌肉的工作方式。

sentences.en: This bionic propulsion is very important clinically to patients.
sentences.zh: 这种仿生推进力在临床上对患者非常重要。

sentences.en: So on the left, you see the bionic device worn by a lady, on the right, a passive device worn by the same lady, that fails to emulate normal muscle function, enabling her to do something everyone should be able to do:
sentences.zh: 因此，在左边，您可以看到一位女士佩戴的仿生设备，在右边，是同一位女士佩戴的被动设备，它无法模拟正常的肌肉功能，使她能够做一些每个人都应该能够做的事情：

sentences.en: go up and down their steps at home. Bionics also allows for extraordinary athletic feats.
sentences.zh: 在家里的台阶上走来走去。仿生学还可以实现非凡的运动壮举。

sentences.en: Here's a gentleman running up a rocky pathway.
sentences.zh: 这是一位绅士在一条岩石小路上奔跑。

sentences.en: This is Steve Martin -- not the comedian -- who lost his legs in a bomb blast in Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 这是史蒂夫·马丁——不是喜剧演员——在阿富汗的一次炸弹爆炸中失去了双腿。

sentences.en: We're also building exoskeletal structures using these same principles, that wrap around the biological limb.
sentences.zh: 我们还使用相同的原理构建包裹生物肢体的外骨骼结构。

sentences.en: This gentleman does not have any leg condition, any disability.
sentences.zh: 这位先生没有任何腿部疾病，也没有任何残疾。

sentences.en: He has a normal physiology, so these exoskeletons are applying muscle-like torques and powers, so that his own muscles need not apply those torques and powers.
sentences.zh: 他有正常的生理机能，所以这些外骨骼正在施加类似肌肉的扭矩和功率，这样他自己的肌肉就不需要施加那些扭矩和功率。

sentences.en: This is the first exoskeleton in history that actually augments human walking.
sentences.zh: 这是历史上第一个真正增强人类行走能力的外骨骼。

sentences.en: It significantly reduces metabolic cost.
sentences.zh: 它显着降低了代谢成本。

sentences.en: It's so profound in its augmentation, that when a normal, healthy person wears the device for 40 minutes and then takes it off, their own biological legs feel ridiculously heavy and awkward.
sentences.zh: 它的增强作用是如此深远，以至于当一个正常健康的人佩戴该设备 40 分钟然后将其摘下时，他们自己的生物腿会感到异常沉重和尴尬。

sentences.en: We're beginning the age in which machines attached to our bodies will make us stronger and faster and more efficient.
sentences.zh: 我们正在开始一个时代，附着在我们身上的机器将使我们变得更强壮、更快、更高效。

sentences.en: Moving on to electrical interface: How do my bionic limbs communicate with my nervous system?
sentences.zh: 继续讨论电气接口：我的仿生肢体如何与我的神经系统进行通信？

sentences.en: Across my residual limb are electrodes that measure the electrical pulse of my muscles.
sentences.zh: 我的残肢上有电极，可以测量我肌肉的电脉冲。

sentences.en: That's communicated to the bionic limb, so when I think about moving my phantom limb, the robot tracks those movement desires.
sentences.zh: 这是与仿生肢体沟通的，所以当我考虑移动我的幻肢时，机器人会跟踪这些运动欲望。

sentences.en: This diagram shows fundamentally how the bionic limb is controlled.
sentences.zh: 该图从根本上显示了仿生肢体是如何控制的。

sentences.en: So we model the missing biological limb, and we've discovered what reflexes occurred, how the reflexes of the spinal cord are controlling the muscles.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们对缺失的生物肢体进行了建模，我们发现了发生了什么反射，脊髓的反射如何控制肌肉。

sentences.en: And that capability is embedded in the chips of the bionic limb.
sentences.zh: 这种能力被嵌入到仿生肢体的芯片中。

sentences.en: What we've done, then, is we modulate the sensitivity of the reflex, the modeled spinal reflex, with the neural signal, so when I relax my muscles in my residual limb, I get very little torque and power,
sentences.zh: 那么，我们所做的就是用神经信号调节反射的敏感性，即模拟脊髓反射，所以当我放松残肢的肌肉时，我得到的扭矩和功率非常小，

sentences.en: but the more I fire my muscles, the more torque I get, and I can even run.
sentences.zh: 但我的肌肉越活跃，获得的扭矩就越大，我什至可以跑步。

sentences.en: And that was the first demonstration of a running gait under neural command.
sentences.zh: 这是神经命令下跑步步态的首次演示。

sentences.en: Feels great. (Applause) We want to go a step further.
sentences.zh: 感觉很棒。 （鼓掌）我们想更进一步。

sentences.en: We want to actually close the loop between the human and the bionic external limb.
sentences.zh: 我们希望真正闭合人类和仿生外肢之间的循环。

sentences.en: We're doing experiments where we're growing nerves, transected nerves, through channels, or micro-channel arrays.
sentences.zh: 我们正在进行实验，通过通道或微通道阵列生长神经、横断神经。

sentences.en: On the other side of the channel, the nerve then attaches to cells, skin cells and muscle cells.
sentences.zh: 在通道的另一侧，神经附着在细胞、皮肤细胞和肌肉细胞上。

sentences.en: In the motor channels, we can sense how the person wishes to move.
sentences.zh: 在运动通道中，我们可以感觉到人希望如何移动。

sentences.en: That can be sent out wirelessly to the bionic limb, then [sensory information] on the bionic limb can be converted to stimulations in adjacent channels, sensory channels.
sentences.zh: 可以无线发送到仿生肢体，然后仿生肢体上的[感觉信息]可以转换为相邻通道、感觉通道的刺激。

sentences.en: So when this is fully developed and for human use, persons like myself will not only have synthetic limbs that move like flesh and bone, but actually feel like flesh and bone.
sentences.zh: 因此，当它完全开发出来并供人类使用时，像我这样的人不仅会拥有像血肉和骨骼一样移动的合成肢体，而且实际上感觉起来也像血肉和骨骼。

sentences.en: This video shows Lisa Mallette, shortly after being fitted with two bionic limbs.
sentences.zh: 这段视频展示了丽莎·马莱特 (Lisa Mallette) 在安装两个仿生肢体后不久的情况。

sentences.en: Indeed, bionics is making a profound difference in people's lives.
sentences.zh: 事实上，仿生学正在给人们的生活带来深刻的改变。

sentences.en: (Video) Lisa Mallette: Oh my God. LM: Oh my God, I can't believe it!
sentences.zh: （视频）丽莎·马莱特：天啊。 LM：天哪，我简直不敢相信！

sentences.en: (Video) (Laughter) LM: It's just like I've got a real leg!
sentences.zh: （视频）（笑声） LM：就像我有一条真正的腿一样！

sentences.en: Woman: Now, don't start running. Man: Now turn around, and do the same thing walking up, but get on your heel to toe, like you would normally just walk on level ground.
sentences.zh: 女：现在，别开始跑步。男：现在转身，做同样的事情向上走，但要从脚跟到脚趾，就像平常在平地上行走一样。

sentences.en: Try to walk right up the hill. LM: Oh my God.
Man: Is it pushing you up? LM: Yes! I'm not even -- I can't even describe it.
Man: It's pushing you right up. Hugh Herr: Next week, I'm visiting the Center -- Thank you. Thank you.
(Applause) Thank you. Next week I'm visiting the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Services, and I'm going to try to convince CMS to grant appropriate code language and pricing,
so this technology can be made available to the patients that need it.
(Applause) Thank you. (Applause) It's not well appreciated, but over half of the world's population suffers from some form of cognitive, emotional, sensory or motor condition,
and because of poor technology, too often, conditions result in disability and a poorer quality of life.
Basic levels of physiological function should be a part of our human rights.
Every person should have the right to live life without disability if they so choose -- the right to live life without severe depression; the right to see a loved one, in the case of seeing-impaired;
or the right to walk or to dance, in the case of limb paralysis or limb amputation.
As a society, we can achieve these human rights, if we accept the proposition that humans are not disabled.
A person can never be broken. Our built environment, our technologies, are broken and disabled.
We the people need not accept our limitations, but can transcend disability through technological innovation.
Indeed, through fundamental advances in bionics in this century, we will set the technological foundation for an enhanced human experience, and we will end disability.
I'd like to finish up with one more story, a beautiful story.
The story of Adrianne Haslet-Davis. Adrianne lost her left leg in the Boston terrorist attack.
I met Adrianne when this photo was taken, at Spaulding Rehabilitation Hospital.
Adrianne is a dancer, a ballroom dancer.
Adrianne breathes and lives dance. It is her expression. It is her art form.
Naturally, when she lost her limb in the Boston terrorist attack, she wanted to return to the dance floor.
After meeting her and driving home in my car, I thought, I'm an MIT professor. I have resources.
Let's build her a bionic limb, to enable her to go back to her life of dance.
I brought in MIT scientists with expertise in prosthetics, robotics, machine learning and biomechanics, and over a 200-day research period, we studied dance.
We brought in dancers with biological limbs, and we studied how they move, what forces they apply on the dance floor, and we took those data, and we put forth fundamental principles of dance,
reflexive dance capability, and we embedded that intelligence into the bionic limb.
Bionics is not only about making people stronger and faster.
Our expression, our humanity can be embedded into electromechanics.
It was 3.5 seconds between the bomb blasts in the Boston terrorist attack.
In 3.5 seconds, the criminals and cowards took Adrianne off the dance floor.
In 200 days, we put her back. We will not be intimidated, brought down, diminished, conquered or stopped by acts of violence.
(Applause) Ladies and gentlemen, please allow me to introduce Adrianne Haslet-Davis,
her first performance since the attack. She's dancing with Christian Lightner.
(Applause) (Music: "Ring My Bell" performed by Enrique Iglesias)
(Applause) Ladies and gentlemen, members of the research team:
Elliott Rouse and Nathan Villagaray-Carski.
Elliott and Nathan. (Applause)
